summary: The reader is built to laugh, cheer, and cry: to love the crew as friends, hate injustice, and feel the hope of a dream chased for decades.

need-to-breathe.why: Luffy sinking helpless in water is built for a brief catch of breath.

hungry.why: Sanji's dishes and the feasts are drawn to make the reader hungry, a running pleasure of the manga.

full.why: Nothing is built to produce this.

thirsty.why: The Alabasta desert is drawn to be felt, a little.

gassy.why: Nothing is built to produce this.

need-to-poop.why: Nothing is built to produce this.

need-to-pee.why: Nothing is built to produce this.

sleepy.why: The manga does not aim to lull.

nauseous.why: Nothing is built to sicken the reader.

urge-to-sneeze.why: Nothing is built to produce this.

urge-to-cough.why: Nothing is built to produce this.

dizzy.why: Luffy's Gear Fourth bouncing and the giant set pieces give a flicker of vertigo.

fatigued.why: The reader is not made to feel exertion.

pain.why: Zoro's chest split by Mihawk and Luffy's beatings are drawn to make the reader wince.

disgusted.why: The Celestial Dragons' slave collars and Caesar's experiments are built to disgust the reader morally and bodily.

itchy.why: Nothing is built to produce this.

tickled.why: Nothing is built to produce this.

over-stimulated.why: The double-page battle spreads are built to overwhelm the eye, briefly.

too-hot-too-cold.why: Drum Island's snow and Punk Hazard's halves are drawn to be felt, slightly.

afraid.why: Arlong, Doflamingo, and Kaido are built to frighten on the crew's behalf, lightened by comedy.

anxious.why: The reader is built to worry for the crew at Sabaody, Marineford, and every climax.

panic.why: The crew scattered by Kuma gives the reader a rush of panic.

sensory-pleasures.why: Feasts and parties are drawn as vicarious pleasure.

aesthetic-pleasures.why: Oda's world design, the islands, ships, and creatures, is built for the reader's pleasure in invention.

piquancy.why: Nothing is built to produce this.

fun-excitement.why: Every island, fight, and gag is built as adventure fun; the manga is a playground for the reader.

orgasm.why: Nothing is built to produce this.

love-romantic.why: Hancock's crush is comic; the manga builds little romantic feeling.

love-family.why: Ace shielding Luffy, Bellemere's death, and Sanji and Zeff are built to touch the reader's family feeling.

grief.why: Ace's death and the Going Merry's funeral are built to make readers cry, and they do.

missing-someone.why: Brook's Bink's Sake and the two-year separation are built to make the reader feel absence.

aroused-sexually.why: Nami's and Robin's drawn figures and Sanji's nosebleeds are built as fan service, mild.

liking-as-a-friend.why: The reader is built to love the Straw Hats as a crew of friends, the manga's central design.

empathy.why: The backstory flashbacks put the reader inside each member's wound before the crew saves them.

compassion.why: Nami's tears under Arlong, Robin's twenty years, and Chopper's exile are built to produce pity that the crew then answers.

grateful.why: Nothing is built to make the reader grateful.

pleasure-from-helping.why: Nothing is built to produce this.

trustful-distrustful.why: The reader is shown traitors and disguised enemies before the crew sees them.

depressed.why: Luffy's breakdown after Ace can lower the reader's mood, briefly.

angry.why: The Celestial Dragons, Arlong, and Doflamingo are built to anger the reader.

envious.why: Nothing is built to produce envy.

jealous-romantic-sexual.why: Nothing is built to produce this.

jealous-friendship.why: Nothing is built to produce this.

hatred.why: Doflamingo, Akainu, and the Celestial Dragons are built to be hated.

contempt.why: The Celestial Dragons' absurd arrogance and Spandam's cowardice are built for the reader's scorn.

resentment.why: Ohara, slavery, Wano's starvation, and Dressrosa's toys are built to make the reader feel injustice as a spur.

proud.why: The crew's triumphs give the reader a borrowed pride.

amused.why: Luffy's faces, Usopp's lies, Chopper's reactions, and Brook's skull jokes are built for laughter on every page.

sense-of-belonging.why: The reader is built to feel a member of the crew and of a fandom; nakama is the word.

lonely.why: Robin's, Brook's, and Chopper's isolations are built to make the reader feel loneliness before it is cured.

judgy-moral-sense.why: Absolute Justice, the Buster Call, and slavery are built to engage the reader's moral judgment on every arc.

admiration.why: Luffy's refusal to fall, Zoro's resolve, and Whitebeard's death standing are built to be admired.

embarrassed.why: Sanji's humiliations and Chopper's dance give secondhand embarrassment.

shame.why: Nothing is built to shame the reader.

guilt.why: Nothing is built to make the reader guilty.

sad.why: Every arc's farewell and flashback is built to make the reader cry.

happy.why: The crew's life aboard is built to make the reader happy to return.

joyful-euphoric.why: Each victory and feast is built as an exultant payoff.

effort.why: More than a thousand chapters ask persistence of a reader.

focused-in-flow.why: The arcs are built to keep the reader turning pages for years.

bored.why: Long arcs can sag, though not by design.

impatient.why: Weekly cliffhangers are built to make the reader impatient for the next chapter.

curious.why: What is One Piece, what happened in the Void Century, who will win: the manga is built on questions decades long.

surprised.why: Sabo alive, Sanji's family, Dragon as father, and each arc's reveals are built to astonish.

awe.why: Whitebeard's power, Zunesha, Enel's ark, and the Red Line are built to produce awe at scale.

skeptical-doubtful.why: The reader doubts Usopp's tales and suspects traitors with the crew.

feeling-of-knowing.why: Oda's long-planted foreshadowing is built to make the reader feel answers almost in reach.

confused.why: The sprawl of factions and powers can confuse, though not by design.

frustrated.why: Ace's death after the rescue is built to frustrate the reader's hope.

uncertain-certain.why: The reader is rarely in doubt that Luffy will win, only how.

understanding.why: Robin's readings and the Void Century reveals are built to give the reader the world's history piece by piece.

inspired.why: The crew's dreams are built to inspire the reader to chase their own.

satisfied.why: Each arc closes with a feast and freed island, but the great question stays open.

foreboding.why: The Will of D. and the coming war are built to make the reader expect a reckoning.

nostalgia.why: Flashbacks and Bink's Sake are built to make the reader feel the weight of the past.

anticipation-suspense.why: Cliffhangers every chapter and every climax are built as suspense.

hope.why: Luffy's dream and the oppressed islands' hope are built to make the reader hope with them, the manga's engine.

schadenfreude.why: Buggy's humiliations and the Celestial Dragon punched are built to be enjoyed.

elevation.why: Whitebeard's death standing, Oden's hour in the pot, and Corazon's sacrifice are built to lift the reader.

infatuation.why: Hancock's crush is comic; the reader is not infatuated.

rage.why: The Celestial Dragons and Akainu are built to make the reader share Luffy's rage.
